newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends sharply higher on planting concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends sharply higher on planting concerns.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended up half their 12-cent limit amid concerns a cold, wet spring would delay corn plantings and ideas a frost in Argentina nipped late seeded crops, traders said.
Frigid weather, rain and snow hit the central U.S. over the weekend and more cold was forecast for Wednesday and Thursday from North Dakota to northern Texas and east to Ohio, meteorologists said.
Traders speculated the cold, wet weather would delay corn plantings and force some farmers to switch intended corn acreage to soybeans.
Soybeans can be planted into July in the Midwest while corn can be sowed only into June.

Old-crop months were supported by talk a leading U.S. analytical firm cut its estimate for Argentine corn production due to a drought late in the growing season. A weekend cold snap in South America further stressed crops, traders said.
USDA's weekly export inspections were also said to be supportive. USDA put inspections at 31.3 million bushels, in line with trade expectations for 32 million to 35 million.
Corn ended 6-1/2 to 5-3/4 cents higher, with May up 6-1/2 at $3.00-3/4 per bushel.
On the day, Prudential Securities bought 3.5 million bushels May, Cargill Investor Services bought 2.5 million July and Merrill Lynch bought 3.5 million May, traders said.

ADM spread two million bushels May/July at 2-1/2 cents, premium July, Dean Witter spread 2.5 million July/May at 2-1/2 cents, premium July and Cargill Inc spread one million bushels December/May at 4-1/2 cents, premium July.

In options trade, Continental Grain bought 600 December $3.60 calls at 5-3/4 cents, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 800 July $3.00 calls at 13 to 13-1/4 cents and FIMAT Futures bought 400 May $2.90 puts at three to 3-1/4 cents.
Corn volume was estimated by CBOT at 80,000 contracts, against Friday's actual volume of 107,605 contracts.
